newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti sells PCs to Piedmont - CEO.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti sells PCs to Piedmont - CEO.

text.p: Italian information technology group Olivetti is selling its personal computers division to a new company Piedmont, in which Olivetti will have a 10 percent stake, chief executive officer Roberto Colaninno said on Monday.
Colaninno told a joint news conference here with U.S. financier Edward Gottesman the PC division was being sold for 250 to 300 billion lire ($159 to $190 million) to the new company.
Gottesman said information on ownership of Piedmont International would be announced in due course.
Gottesman and Colaninno told the news conference that Gianmario Rossignolo, chairman of AB Electrolux unit Zanussi, had agreed to become executive chairman of Piedmont.

As part of the deal, the Olivetti brand would be licensed to Piedmont for four years. Olivetti's personal computers plant Scarmagno would stay open as part of the deal and it would remain owned by Olivetti and leased to Piedmont for four years.
Gottesman said: "There is no intention of moving any manufacturing out of Scarmagno."
Colaninno said after two years Olivetti had the option to sell its 10 percent to Piedmont, which Piedmont had to buy.
"A formula has been decided to determine the price," he said.

Olivetti has been seeking a buyer since late last year for the PC division, the sector which, under former chairman Carlo De Benedetti, made the company's name in the 1980s but which has since suffered losses in the competitive climate of the 1990s.
